title: Async and Await
description: Use cooperative concurrency for I/O while handling tasks, cancellation, timeouts, and blocking work safely.

sections.title: Core mental model
sections.learning_objective: Explain coroutines and the event loop
sections.markdown: Calling an `async def` function creates a coroutine object; its body runs only when awaited or scheduled. The event loop advances one task until it reaches an `await` that can suspend, then gives another ready task time to run. This is cooperative concurrency, ideal for many waiting operations—not automatic CPU parallelism.

examples.code:
import asyncio

async def fetch(name):
    await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
    return name.upper()

print(asyncio.run(fetch('forge')))

sections.title: Operations and trade-offs
sections.learning_objective: Run independent I/O with tasks and gather
sections.markdown: Use `asyncio.create_task()` when work should start before it is awaited. `asyncio.gather()` waits for independent awaitables while preserving input order in its results. Blocking IO such as `time.sleep()` or synchronous file/network I/O freezes the event-loop thread; choose an async client or use `asyncio.to_thread()` for suitable blocking functions.

examples.code:
import asyncio

async def main():
    async with asyncio.timeout(1):
        values = await asyncio.gather(asyncio.sleep(0, result=2), asyncio.sleep(0, result=3))
    print(sum(values))

asyncio.run(main())

sections.title: Worked practice
sections.learning_objective: Trace the concept on concrete data.
sections.markdown: Work from the input and state the invariant before coding. Timeouts and cancellation are normal control flow. `asyncio.timeout()` bounds an operation, while task cancellation raises `CancelledError` at an await point. Use `try/finally` to release resources and normally re-raise cancellation. Common mistakes include creating but never awaiting a coroutine, sequentially awaiting independent work, swallowing cancellation, and using async syntax for CPU-bound loops. For an interview, narrate the observation, the rule you are applying, and the resulting value. That sequence makes reasoning inspectable and exposes hidden assumptions.
